transcript.text: My Samsung dishwasher DW60M6050FS keeps showing 4C and beeping, won't do anything

The 4C code on your Samsung dishwasher indicates a water supply issue - specifically that little or no fresh water is entering the machine. This is often caused by a simple blockage or a closed tap rather than a broken part. Before we look at internal components, please check these owner-safe steps:
1. Ensure the isolation tap (the small valve on the wall) where the dishwasher hose connects is fully open.
2. Check that the inlet hose isn't kinked behind the machine.
3. Unscrew the inlet hose from the back of the dishwasher (have a towel ready for water). Look into the inlet port on the machine; there is a small mesh filter here. If it's blocked with grit or scale, clean it under the tap. If it was already clean, note that.
4. Reconnect the hose, ensure the door is shut firmly until it clicks (a loose door can prevent filling), and try starting a programme again. Let me know if the water starts flowing normally after these checks, or if you found the filter blocked.

Found it - the valve under the sink (the screwdriver slot type) was at 90 degrees, so it was turned off. I turned it on and the dishwasher now fills and runs normally. No kinks in the hose either. I didn't take the hose off to look at the filter.

That’s excellent news. It sounds like the dishwasher was simply locked out because the water supply was turned off at the tap. Since it is now filling and running normally, there is no need to check the inlet filter or replace any parts. To stop this from happening again, just keep an eye on that isolation valve under the sink—accidentally bumping it closed is a common cause of these '4C' errors. If you have any other questions about your Samsung dishwasher, just let me know.

candidates: Water supply / isolation tap / inlet hose / inlet filter (check first) (high)
Door not latched properly or door wiring issue (medium)

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Samsung; model DW60M6050FS; code 4C.
The fault they reported is: "beeping, won't do anything". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
The most likely cause, chosen from the evidence: water supply / isolation tap / inlet hose / inlet filter (check first). Lead with it and why it fits what they said; mention at most one alternative.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
